en.v: 25 cm skillet, food processor, 2840 ml or 3780 ml stainless steel pot

sk.v: Panvica 25 cm, kuchynský robot, nerezový hrniec 2840 ml alebo 3780 ml

en.v: Uncut bagels keep for up to 48 hours in a paper bag (or loosely wrapped in parchment); slice and toast briefly to serve.

sk.v: Nenakrájané bagely vydržia až 48 hodín v papierovom vrecku (alebo voľne zabalené v papieri na pečenie); pred podávaním ich prekrojte a krátko opečte.

en.t: 170 g cold water
100 g bread flour (spooned)
355 g bread flour (spooned)
15 g sugar (1 tbsp)
2 1/2 tsp (9 g) Diamond Crystal kosher salt; for table salt, use half as much by volume or use the same weight
1 tsp (4 g) instant dry yeast, such as SAF; not RapidRise or active dry
100 g water
30 g barley malt syrup (4 tsp (20 ml))

sk.t: 100 g chlebová múka (do odmerky nasypaná lyžicou)
355 g chlebová múka (do odmerky nasypaná lyžicou)
2 ½ ČL (9 g) hrubozrnná soľ Diamond Crystal (pri jemnej soli dáme objemovo polovicu, hmotnostne rovnako)
1 ČL (4 g) instantné sušené droždie, napr. SAF (nie RapidRise ani aktívne sušené droždie)
30 g jačmenný sladový sirup (4 ČL (20 ml))

en.t: 1. For the Yukone: In a 25 cm skillet, whisk water and flour over medium heat until thick, like mashed potatoes, about 2 minutes. Scrape onto a plate, spread into a 2.5 cm layer, cover and cool to about 23 °C, around 30 minutes.

2. For the Dough: Pulse flour, sugar, salt, and instant yeast in a food processor fitted with a metal blade. Once combined, add cooled yukone and water. Process until dough is silky smooth, and a small piece can be stretched into a sheet without tearing, about 90 seconds. The exact timing will vary with the power and capacity of a given machine. For smaller machines, the reduced capacity and power will necessitate dividing dough in half to process in stages.

3. To Shape: Turn dough onto a clean, un-floured surface, and divide into 8 roughly equal portions (about 85 g each) and cover with plastic. Cup a portion of dough beneath your palm and work in quick, circular motions to form a tight ball, with only a tiny seam along the bottom. If the seam is large or irregular, continue rounding until the bottom is nearly smooth. Keep the shaped dough covered in plastic and let rest 15 minutes.

4. To form the bagels, poke a hole into the center of each portion with a damp fingertip, then gently stretch into an 8.5 cm ring, wetting your hands in cold water as needed to prevent sticking. Arrange on a well-greased, parchment-lined half sheet pan, cover with plastic, and refrigerate 24 to 36 hours, depending on your schedule.

5. To Boil: Adjust oven rack to lower-middle position and preheat to 220 °C (fan 200 °C). Fill a stainless steel pot with about 7.5 cm of water, stir in barley malt syrup, and bring to a boil over high heat. Meanwhile, line a baking sheet or cutting board with a thick layer of paper towels. Working two or three at a time, boil the bagels about 30 seconds per side. Drain on paper towels for two or three seconds, then transfer to a parchment-lined half sheet pan. (If left on the paper towels too long, the bagels will stick; if this happens, quickly dip the bagel back into the hot water, and the wet paper towel will peel right off.)

6. To Finish: Bake the bagels until blistered and golden brown all over, about 25 minutes. Cool at least 15 minutes. To serve, split horizontally with a serrated knife. Uncut, bagels can be stored up to 48 hours in a paper bag (or loosely wrapped in parchment), then sliced and briefly toasted to serve.

1. Yukone (zápara): v panvici s priemerom 25 cm šľaháme na strednom ohni vodu a múku, kým zmes nezhustne ako zemiaková kaša, asi 2 minúty. Zoškrabeme na tanier, rozotrieme do vrstvy hrubej 2,5 cm, prikryjeme a necháme vychladnúť asi na 23 °C, približne 30 minút.

2. Cesto: múku, cukor, soľ a instantné droždie premiešame pulzmi v kuchynskom robote s kovovým nožom. Keď sa spoja, pridáme vychladnutú záparu a vodu. Mixujeme, kým cesto nie je hodvábne hladké a malý kúsok sa nedá natiahnuť na blanu bez roztrhnutia, asi 90 sekúnd. Presný čas sa bude líšiť podľa výkonu a kapacity robota. Pri menších robotoch si nižšia kapacita a výkon vyžiadajú rozdeliť cesto na polovicu a spracovať ho po častiach.

3. Tvarovanie: cesto vyklopíme na čistú nepomúčenú plochu, rozdelíme na 8 zhruba rovnakých dielov (každý asi 85 g) a prikryjeme fóliou. Diel cesta prikryjeme dlaňou a rýchlymi krúživými pohybmi vytvarujeme pevnú guľku s len drobným spojom na spodku. Ak je spoj veľký alebo nepravidelný, guľku tvarujeme ďalej, kým spodok nie je takmer hladký. Vytvarované cesto necháme prikryté fóliou a 15 minút odpočívať.

4. Na tvarovanie bagiel urobíme navlhčeným končekom prsta do stredu každého dielu otvor, potom ho jemne natiahneme na krúžok s priemerom 8,5 cm; ruky podľa potreby namáčame do studenej vody, aby sa cesto nelepilo. Uložíme na dobre vymastený plech (polovičný) vystlaný papierom na pečenie, prikryjeme fóliou a necháme v chladničke 24 až 36 hodín podľa nášho časového plánu.

5. Varenie: rošt nastavíme do polohy pod stredom rúry a rúru rozohrejeme na 220 °C (teplovzdušnú na 200 °C). Nerezový hrniec naplníme asi 7,5 cm vody, vmiešame jačmenný sladový sirup a na silnom ohni privedieme do varu. Medzitým plech alebo dosku na krájanie vystelieme hrubou vrstvou papierových utierok. Bagely varíme po dvoch či troch asi 30 sekúnd z každej strany. Necháme ich odkvapkať na papierových utierkach dve či tri sekundy, potom ich preložíme na polovičný plech vystlaný papierom na pečenie. (Ak ich necháme na papierových utierkach príliš dlho, bagely sa prilepia; ak sa to stane, bagel rýchlo ponoríme späť do horúcej vody a mokrá utierka sa hneď odlepí.)

6. Dokončenie: bagely pečieme, kým nie sú pokryté pľuzgierikmi a celé zlatistohnedé, asi 25 minút. Necháme chladnúť aspoň 15 minút. Pri podávaní ich zúbkovaným nožom vodorovne prekrojíme. Neprekrojené bagely môžeme uchovávať až 48 hodín v papierovom vrecku (alebo voľne zabalené v papieri na pečenie), potom ich nakrájame a pred podávaním krátko opečieme.

cat.en: Pre-shape the dough into balls, then stretch them into rings; it is gentle on the gluten and gives seamless bagels.
cat.sk: Cesto najprv vytvarujte do guľôčok a potom ich roztiahnite na kruhy; šetrí to lepok a bagely nebudú mať spoj.

tip.en: Knead the raisins in by hand so they stay intact, and shape each portion until there is almost no seam underneath; the raisins can otherwise cause blowouts as the bagels rise.
tip.sk: Hrozienka zapracujte do cesta ručne, aby zostali celé, a každú porciu tvarujte, kým zospodu nezmizne takmer celý šev; inak môžu hrozienka pri kysnutí bagel roztrhnúť.

en.t: 425 g all-purpose flour, such as Gold Medal
1 3/4 tsp (7 g) Diamond Crystal kosher salt; for table salt, use the same weight or half as much by volume
1 1/8 tsp (6 g) baking soda
510 g low-fat cultured buttermilk, well shaken

sk.t: 425 g hladká múka, napr. Gold Medal
1 ¾ ČL (7 g) hrubozrnná soľ Diamond Crystal (pri jemnej soli rovnaká hmotnosť alebo objemovo polovica)
510 g low-fat cultured buttermilk, well shaken

en.t: 1. Adjust oven rack to middle position and preheat to 230 °C (fan 210 °C) at least 15 minutes in advance. Roughly cover bottom of deep 25 cm cast-iron or enameled Dutch oven with sheet of parchment paper; no need to trim.

2. Combine flour, salt, and baking soda in a large bowl and whisk for 1 full minute to combine. Stir in buttermilk with flexible spatula until dough is fully moistened and no pockets of flour remain. For extra-fluffy results, stop folding as soon as dough comes together. For extra-chewy results, fold dough about 20 seconds more. Scrape sticky dough into prepared Dutch oven and smooth with spatula into rough boule-like shape. Score deeply into quarters with sharp knife or razor, cleaning the blade between each slice.

3. Cover and bake until well risen and golden, 45 minutes. Remove lid and continue baking until chestnut brown, with an internal temperature of 99 °C, 12 to 15 minutes longer. Invert onto a wire rack, discard parchment, turn right side up, and cool until crumb has set, about 30 minutes. Cut thick slices to accompany hearty soups and stews, or slice thinly for sandwiches. (This will be easier if bread cools at least 2 hours.) Store up to 24 hours in an airtight container and toast to freshen bread before serving.

1. Rošt nastavíme do stredu rúry a rúru rozohrejeme na 230 °C (teplovzdušnú na 210 °C) aspoň 15 minút vopred. Dno hlbokého liatinového alebo smaltovaného hrnca s priemerom 25 cm zhruba prikryjeme papierom na pečenie; netreba ho zarovnávať.

2. Vo veľkej mise spojíme múku, soľ a sódu bikarbónu a celú 1 minútu miešame metličkou, aby sa spojili. Pružnou stierkou vmiešame cmar, kým cesto nie je úplne zvlhčené a nezostanú v ňom kapsy múky. Ak chceme mimoriadne nadýchaný výsledok, prestaneme miešať, len čo sa cesto spojí. Ak chceme mimoriadne žuvací výsledok, cesto prekladáme ešte asi 20 sekúnd. Lepkavé cesto zoškrabeme do pripraveného hrnca a stierkou ho uhladíme do približného tvaru okrúhleho bochníka. Ostrým nožom alebo žiletkou ho hlboko narežeme na štvrtiny; čepeľ medzi jednotlivými rezmi očistíme.

3. Prikryjeme a pečieme, kým dobre nenakysne a nie je zlatistý, 45 minút. Odkryjeme a pečieme ďalej, kým nie je gaštanovohnedý s vnútornou teplotou 99 °C, ešte 12 až 15 minút. Vyklopíme na mriežku, papier vyhodíme, obrátime správnou stranou nahor a necháme chladnúť, kým striedka nestuhne, asi 30 minút. Hrubé krajce nakrájame k výdatným polievkam a dusenému mäsu alebo tenko na sendviče. (Pôjde to ľahšie, ak chlieb chladne aspoň 2 hodiny.) Uchovávame až 24 hodín v uzavretej nádobe a pred podávaním ho opečieme, aby sa osviežil.

en.v: 23 × 13 cm metal loaf pan, 25 cm nonstick or cast iron skillet, potato masher or large fork

sk.v: Kovová forma na chlieb 23 × 13 cm, nepriľnavá alebo liatinová panvica 25 cm, šťuchadlo na zemiaky alebo veľká vidlička

en.v: The cooled loaf can be covered tightly with plastic wrap or stored in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 4 days or frozen for up to 2 months.

sk.v: Vychladnutý bochník môžeme pevne zabaliť do fólie alebo uchovávať v uzatvárateľnej nádobe pri izbovej teplote až 4 dni alebo zmraziť až na 2 mesiace.

c.t: To toast the coconut, spread it on a lined rimmed baking sheet and bake on the middle rack at 175 °C, stirring every 5 minutes, until mixed golden brown and white, about 15 minutes; cool on the sheet.

Kokos opražíte tak, že ho rozložíte na plech s okrajom vystlaný papierom a pečiete v strede rúry pri 175 °C, každých 5 minút premiešate, kým nie je čiastočne zlatohnedý a čiastočne biely, asi 15 minút; nechajte vychladnúť na plechu.

en.t: 225 g all-purpose flour
1 tsp (3 g) Diamond Crystal kosher salt; if using table salt use half as much by volume
3/4 tsp (4.5 g) baking soda
1/2 tsp (2 g) baking powder
6 very ripe (lightly speckled to heavily speckled) bananas, peeled (2 left whole, 4 halved lengthwise and halved crosswise)
8 tbsp (115 g) unsalted butter, divided
198 g packed dark brown sugar
2 large eggs (≈100 g without shell), lightly beaten
1 tsp (5 ml) vanilla extract
100 g walnuts, toasted, optional
60 g packed sweetened shredded coconut, toasted
85 g chocolate chips, optional

sk.t: 1 ČL (3 g) hrubozrnná soľ Diamond Crystal (pri jemnej soli objemovo polovica)
½ ČL (2 g) prášok do pečiva
6 veľmi zrelých banánov (so slabými až hustými hnedými škvrnami), ošúpaných (2 celé, 4 pozdĺžne a priečne rozpolené)
2 veľké vajcia (≈100 g bez škrupiny), zľahka rozšľahané
60 g sladená kokosová strúhanka, natlačená, opražená

en.t: 1. Adjust oven rack to middle position and heat oven to 175 °C (fan 155 °C). Spray bottom and sides of a 23 × 13 cm metal loaf pan with vegetable oil spray.
2. In a medium bowl, whisk the flour, salt, baking soda, and baking powder until combined; set aside. In a large bowl, use a potato masher to mash the 2 whole bananas until fairly smooth; set aside.

3. In a 25 cm nonstick or cast iron skillet, heat 2 tbsp (28 g) butter over medium-high heat until melted. Add banana slices flat side down and cook until glossy, golden brown, and softened, flipping slices as needed, 4 to 6 minutes. Transfer to a bowl.

4. In the now-empty skillet, add the remaining butter and cook over medium-high heat, stirring and swirling skillet constantly with rubber spatula, until butter is light golden brown and has a nutty aroma, 2 to 4 minutes. Return the browned bananas to the skillet and continue to cook, stirring and flipping the banana mixture frequently until the bananas are mostly broken down and the mixture turns dark golden brown and has a deep caramelized nutty banana aroma, 6 to 8 minutes. Off heat stir in the brown sugar, return to heat and cook, stirring frequently, until sugar is fully dissolved and the syrupy mixture gently bubbles, about 1 minute. Transfer the banana mixture to a large bowl with the mashed fresh bananas. Let sit until cooled slightly, for 10 minutes.

5. Using a potato masher, mash the banana mixture until mostly smooth. Whisk in egg and vanilla until combined. Using a spatula, stir in flour mixture until just combined. Fold in walnuts, coconut and/or chocolate chips, if using. Use a rubber spatula to scrape the batter into greased loaf pan and smooth top.

1. Rošt nastavíme do stredu rúry a rúru rozohrejeme na 175 °C (teplovzdušnú na 155 °C). Dno a boky kovovej formy na biskupský chlebíček s rozmermi 23 × 13 cm vystriekame olejovým sprejom.

2. V stredne veľkej mise metličkou premiešame múku, soľ, sódu bikarbónu a prášok do pečiva, kým sa nespoja; odložíme. Vo veľkej mise roztlačíme 2 celé banány štuchadlom na zemiaky na takmer hladkú kašu; odložíme.

3. V panvici s nepriľnavým povrchom alebo liatinovej panvici s priemerom 25 cm rozpustíme na stredne silnom až silnom ohni 1⅔ PL (24 g) masla. Pridáme plátky banánov plochou stranou nadol a opekáme, kým nie sú lesklé, zlatistohnedé a mäkké; podľa potreby ich obraciame, 4 až 6 minút. Preložíme do misky.

4. Do vyprázdnenej panvice dáme zvyšné maslo a na stredne silnom až silnom ohni ho za stáleho miešania gumenou stierkou a krúženia panvicou zohrievame, kým nie je svetlo zlatistohnedé a nevonia orieškovo, 2 až 4 minúty. Opečené banány vrátime do panvice a ďalej ich za častého miešania a obracania varíme, kým sa banány takmer celkom nerozpadnú a zmes nie je tmavozlatistohnedá s výraznou karamelovo-orieškovou banánovou vôňou, 6 až 8 minút. Mimo ohňa vmiešame hnedý cukor, vrátime na oheň a za častého miešania varíme, kým sa cukor úplne nerozpustí a sirupová zmes jemne nebuble, asi 1 minútu. Banánovú zmes preložíme do veľkej misy k roztlačeným čerstvým banánom. Necháme mierne vychladnúť, 10 minút.

5. Banánovú zmes štuchadlom na zemiaky roztlačíme na takmer hladkú hmotu. Metličkou vmiešame vajce a vanilku, kým sa nespoja. Stierkou vmiešame zmes múky, len kým sa nespojí. Ak ich používame, zľahka vmiešame vlašské orechy, kokos a/alebo kúsky čokolády. Cesto gumenou stierkou zoškrabeme do vymastenej formy a vrch uhladíme.
6. Pečieme, kým banánový chlebíček nie je zlatistohnedý a špáradlo alebo nôž zapichnutý do stredu nevyjde čistý, 50 až 60 minút. Chlebíček preložíme na mriežku a necháme 15 minút chladnúť vo forme.
7. Chňapkami opatrne otočíme formu na bok a chlebíček z nej vyberieme. Necháme ho na mriežke chladnúť ešte aspoň 1 hodinu. Preložíme na dosku, nakrájame a podávame.

en.t: 1. Preheat the oven to 190 °C (fan 170 °C). Lightly grease a 23 cm square or round pan (a cast iron skillet will work fine, too), a shallow 1420 ml casserole dish, or a standard muffin pan.
2. Weigh your flour and cornmeal. In a medium bowl, whisk together the flour, cornmeal, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt.
3. In another bowl or large measuring cup, whisk together the milk, melted butter, vegetable oil, and egg.

c.t: Most all-purpose flour is not high-protein enough; without a high-protein all-purpose flour, use bread flour.

Baked baking soda instead of lye: bake 115 g baking soda spread thinly on a rimmed baking sheet at 175 °C for 1 hour and cool. Bring 1920 ml water with it to a boil in a large enamelled pot, then keep at a gentle simmer, covered; set a bowl of 945 ml cold water nearby.

Wearing gloves, dip each pretzel bottom side up in the soda bath for 30 to 40 seconds, then in the cold water for 30 to 40 seconds, and set it on a rack. Salt them and bake until dark brown, 12 to 14 minutes; mist with water and bake 30 seconds more for a glossy sheen.

Lye safety: food-grade lye and pretzel salt are sold online or in baking supply stores. Always wear gloves and eye protection, and always add lye to water, never water to lye. Use a non-reactive container (plastic, stainless steel or glass); lye stains wood, aluminium and other surfaces, so work on lined baking sheets.

Wipe spills with a damp sponge (or one dipped in white vinegar to neutralise the lye). The bath can be reused for 3 or 4 batches. The used 4% solution can be poured down the sink with cold water running.
Väčšina hladkej múky nemá dosť bielkovín; bez hladkej múky s vysokým obsahom bielkovín použite chlebovú múku.

Pečená sóda namiesto lúhu: 115 g sódy bikarbóny rozložte v tenkej vrstve na plech s okrajom, pečte pri 175 °C 1 hodinu a nechajte vychladnúť. Vo veľkom smaltovanom hrnci ju s 1920 ml vody priveďte do varu, potom udržiavajte pod pokrievkou mierny var; vedľa pripravte misku s 945 ml studenej vody.

V rukaviciach ponorte každý praclík spodnou stranou nahor na 30 až 40 sekúnd do sódového kúpeľa, potom na 30 až 40 sekúnd do studenej vody a položte ho na mriežku. Posoľte a pečte dotmavohneda, 12 až 14 minút; postriekajte vodou a pečte ešte 30 sekúnd, aby sa leskli.

Bezpečnosť pri lúhu: potravinársky lúh a soľ na praclíky kúpite online alebo v obchodoch pre pekárov. Vždy noste rukavice a ochranu očí a vždy pridávajte lúh do vody, nikdy vodu do lúhu. Použite nereaktívnu nádobu (plast, nerez alebo sklo); lúh zafarbí drevo, hliník aj iné povrchy, preto pracujte na plechoch vystlaných papierom.

Rozliate kvapky utrite vlhkou špongiou (alebo špongiou namočenou v bielom octe, ktorý lúh neutralizuje). Kúpeľ môžete použiť na 3 alebo 4 dávky. Použitý 4 % roztok môžete vyliať do drezu pri tečúcej studenej vode.

en.t: 1. For the Poolish: In a medium bowl, whisk together flour and yeast to combine. Add water and, using a dough whisk or wooden spoon, stir until combined and no dry bits remain. Cover tightly and let sit at warm room temperature (22 to 25 °C) until dough is bubbly and has expanded by about half, 3 to 4 hours. Refrigerate for at least 8 hours or up to 24 hours.

2. For the Dough: Add water and butter to bowl with the poolish and, using a dough whisk or wooden spoon, stir until mixture is mostly uniform. In a medium bowl, whisk to combine flour and salt. Add flour mixture to the poolish, water, and butter mixture and knead by hand until shaggy but uniform dough forms. Cover well and let sit at warm room temperature (22 to 25 °C) for 30 minutes.
3. Using slightly moistened hands, knead dough in bowl until uniform in texture, 15 to 30 seconds. Cover well and let sit until puffy and expanded by about half, 60 to 90 minutes.

4. To Form the Pretzels: Line a rimmed baking sheet with a silicone baking mat or parchment paper lightly coated with nonstick cooking spray. Lightly flour top of dough, then transfer to a lightly-floured work surface. Using a dough scraper, divide dough into 6 equal wedges of about 88 g each. Starting with the pointy end of the wedge, roll each wedge into a log about 7.5 cm long, pinching the edge of the rolled-up log along its length to seal. (Do not pinch the log's ends closed.) Cover the logs with an inverted container large enough to contain them all without touching, or a clean plastic garbage bag.

5. Clear your countertop of any flour, then, working one log at a time, roll each log into a 46 cm-long rope of even thickness, rolling from the center out to press out any large bubbles. (If the dough sticks to your hands or countertop, lightly flour your hands and not the dough itself; in order to roll the dough evenly, you need friction between the dough and countertop. If the dough begins to slide around on the countertop, lightly mist your hands with water using a spray bottle.)

6. Taper the outer 15 cm on either end of the rope slightly and continue rolling until the rope is 61 cm total. (Be sure to measure the dough after it has sat for a few seconds; if the rope shrinks after sitting for a few seconds, allow the dough to rest for several minutes, then resume rolling until it is 61 cm long.)

7. Lay the rope on the countertop and draw the two ends toward you to form a U-shape. Cross the two ends of the rope over themselves twice, then fold this bundle over itself toward the bend of the U so that the two ends of the rope just overlap the curve. Adjust the placement of the tips so that 3 even windows form, then press the tips down to seal. Transfer the pretzel to the prepared baking sheet and cover loosely with a clean plastic garbage bag. Repeat with the remaining logs, spacing the pretzels evenly apart on the baking sheet.
8. Transfer the loosely covered baking sheet to the refrigerator and chill for at least 2 hours and up to 24 hours.

9. Adjust oven rack to middle position and preheat oven to 205 °C (fan 185 °C). While the oven preheats, remove the bag from the baking sheet of pretzels and allow pretzels to sit in the fridge uncovered, at least 30 minutes (and up to an hour).

10. For Dipping the Pretzels: If using a lye dip, set a wire rack inside a rimmed baking sheet lined with parchment; spray rack with nonstick cooking spray. Line a second baking sheet with parchment and place it next to the first one. In a large, non-reactive container (such as a Pyrex, glass, or stainless steel bowl or baking dish), add the water. Set the container in the center of the second pan. Wearing gloves and protective eyewear, sprinkle lye over the surface of the water and allow to dissolve, about 5 minutes. (It is very important you put the full amount of water in the container first and then add the lye; if you put the lye in the container and then pour water on top you could cause a violent reaction.) Cover the container loosely with parchment while the oven heats.

11. Wearing gloves and protective eyewear, transfer one pretzel to the lye bath, bottom side up, and let sit for 30 to 40 seconds. (If necessary, use a non-reactive spoon to gently keep the pretzel fully submerged.) Using gloved hands, transfer the pretzel face up to the rack to drain. Repeat with the remaining pretzels. When all the pretzels have been dipped, transfer them back to the original rimmed baking sheet face up and spaced evenly apart. Sprinkle pretzels evenly with pretzel salt and transfer to oven. Bake until dark brown, 12 to 14 minutes. (The lye-dipped pretzels will naturally be darker than the ones dipped in baking soda.) Using a spray bottle, mist pretzels lightly with water and return to oven until the pretzels have a glossy sheen, 30 seconds.
12. Remove pretzels from oven and allow to cool for 5 minutes before serving.

c.t: 1. For the Poolish: In a medium bowl, whisk together flour and yeast to combine. Add water and, using a dough whisk or wooden spoon, stir until combined and no dry bits remain. Cover tightly and let sit at warm room temperature (22 to 25 °C) until dough is bubbly and has expanded by about half, 3 to 4 hours. Refrigerate for at least 8 hours or up to 24 hours.

2. For the Dough: Add water and butter to bowl with the poolish and, using a dough whisk or wooden spoon, stir until mixture is mostly uniform. In a medium bowl, whisk to combine flour and salt. Add flour mixture to the poolish, water, and butter mixture and knead by hand until shaggy but uniform dough forms. Cover well and let sit at warm room temperature (22 to 25 °C) for 30 minutes.
3. Using slightly moistened hands, knead dough in bowl until uniform in texture, 15 to 30 seconds. Cover well and let sit until puffy and expanded by about half, 60 to 90 minutes.

4. To Form the Pretzels: Line a rimmed baking sheet with a silicone baking mat or parchment paper lightly coated with nonstick cooking spray. Lightly flour top of dough, then transfer to a lightly-floured work surface. Using a dough scraper, divide dough into 6 equal wedges of about 88 g each. Starting with the pointy end of the wedge, roll each wedge into a log about 7.5 cm long, pinching the edge of the rolled-up log along its length to seal. (Do not pinch the log's ends closed.) Cover the logs with an inverted container large enough to contain them all without touching, or a clean plastic garbage bag.

5. Clear your countertop of any flour, then, working one log at a time, roll each log into a 46 cm-long rope of even thickness, rolling from the center out to press out any large bubbles. (If the dough sticks to your hands or countertop, lightly flour your hands and not the dough itself; in order to roll the dough evenly, you need friction between the dough and countertop. If the dough begins to slide around on the countertop, lightly mist your hands with water using a spray bottle.)

6. Taper the outer 15 cm on either end of the rope slightly and continue rolling until the rope is 61 cm total. (Be sure to measure the dough after it has sat for a few seconds; if the rope shrinks after sitting for a few seconds, allow the dough to rest for several minutes, then resume rolling until it is 61 cm long.)

7. Lay the rope on the countertop and draw the two ends toward you to form a U-shape. Cross the two ends of the rope over themselves twice, then fold this bundle over itself toward the bend of the U so that the two ends of the rope just overlap the curve. Adjust the placement of the tips so that 3 even windows form, then press the tips down to seal. Transfer the pretzel to the prepared baking sheet and cover loosely with a clean plastic garbage bag. Repeat with the remaining logs, spacing the pretzels evenly apart on the baking sheet.
8. Transfer the loosely covered baking sheet to the refrigerator and chill for at least 2 hours and up to 24 hours.

9. Adjust oven rack to middle position and preheat oven to 205 °C (fan 185 °C). While the oven preheats, remove the bag from the baking sheet of pretzels and allow pretzels to sit in the fridge uncovered, at least 30 minutes (and up to an hour).

10. For Dipping the Pretzels: If using a lye dip, set a wire rack inside a rimmed baking sheet lined with parchment; spray rack with nonstick cooking spray. Line a second baking sheet with parchment and place it next to the first one. In a large, non-reactive container (such as a Pyrex, glass, or stainless steel bowl or baking dish), add the water. Set the container in the center of the second pan. Wearing gloves and protective eyewear, sprinkle lye over the surface of the water and allow to dissolve, about 5 minutes. (It is very important you put the full amount of water in the container first and then add the lye; if you put the lye in the container and then pour water on top you could cause a violent reaction.) Cover the container loosely with parchment while the oven heats.

11. Wearing gloves and protective eyewear, transfer one pretzel to the lye bath, bottom side up, and let sit for 30 to 40 seconds. (If necessary, use a non-reactive spoon to gently keep the pretzel fully submerged.) Using gloved hands, transfer the pretzel face up to the rack to drain. Repeat with the remaining pretzels. When all the pretzels have been dipped, transfer them back to the original rimmed baking sheet face up and spaced evenly apart. Sprinkle pretzels evenly with pretzel salt and transfer to oven. Bake until dark brown, 12 to 14 minutes. (The lye-dipped pretzels will naturally be darker than the ones dipped in baking soda.) Using a spray bottle, mist pretzels lightly with water and return to oven until the pretzels have a glossy sheen, 30 seconds.
12. Remove pretzels from oven and allow to cool for 5 minutes before serving.

1. Poolish: v stredne veľkej mise metličkou premiešame múku a droždie. Pridáme vodu a metličkou na cesto alebo varechou miešame, kým sa nespojí a nezostanú suché kúsky. Tesne prikryjeme a necháme pri teplej izbovej teplote (22 až 25 °C), kým cesto nie je bublinkové a nezväčší objem asi o polovicu, 3 až 4 hodiny. Dáme do chladničky aspoň na 8 hodín alebo najviac na 24 hodín.

2. Cesto: do misy s poolishom pridáme vodu a maslo a metličkou na cesto alebo varechou miešame, kým zmes nie je takmer jednotná. V stredne veľkej mise metličkou premiešame múku a soľ. Múčnu zmes pridáme k zmesi poolishu, vody a masla a rukou miesime, kým nevznikne strapaté, ale jednotné cesto. Dobre prikryjeme a necháme pri teplej izbovej teplote (22 až 25 °C) 30 minút.
3. Mierne navlhčenými rukami miesime cesto v mise, kým nemá jednotnú štruktúru, 15 až 30 sekúnd. Dobre prikryjeme a necháme, kým nie je nadýchané a nezväčší objem asi o polovicu, 60 až 90 minút.

4. Tvarovanie praclíkov: plech s okrajom vystelieme silikónovou podložkou alebo papierom na pečenie zľahka vystriekaným sprejom proti prilepeniu. Vrch cesta zľahka pomúčime a preložíme na zľahka pomúčenú pracovnú plochu. Škrabkou na cesto ho rozdelíme na 6 rovnakých klinov, každý asi 88 g. Každý klin zvinieme od špicatého konca do valčeka dlhého asi 7,5 cm a okraj zvinutého valčeka po celej dĺžke stlačíme, aby sa uzavrel. (Konce valčeka nezatláčame.) Valčeky prikryjeme obrátenou nádobou dostatočne veľkou, aby sa do nej zmestili všetky bez dotyku, alebo čistým igelitovým vrecom.

5. Z pracovnej dosky odstránime všetku múku a potom po jednom vyvaľkáme každý valček na rovnomerne hrubý povraz dlhý 46 cm; vaľkáme od stredu von, aby sme vytlačili väčšie bubliny. (Ak sa cesto lepí na ruky alebo dosku, zľahka pomúčime ruky, nie samotné cesto; aby sa cesto vaľkalo rovnomerne, potrebujeme trenie medzi cestom a doskou. Ak sa cesto začne po doske šmýkať, ruky zľahka navlhčíme vodou z rozprašovača.)

6. Vonkajších 15 cm na oboch koncoch povrazu mierne zúžime a vaľkáme ďalej, kým povraz nemá celkovo 61 cm. (Cesto meriame až po niekoľkých sekundách odpočinku; ak sa povraz po chvíli scvrkne, necháme cesto niekoľko minút odpočívať a potom vaľkáme ďalej, kým nemá 61 cm.)

7. Povraz položíme na dosku a oba konce pritiahneme k sebe do tvaru U. Konce povrazu dvakrát prekrížime a tento zväzok preložíme smerom k ohybu U tak, aby konce povrazu len prekrývali oblúk. Polohu koncov upravíme tak, aby vznikli 3 rovnaké okienka, a konce pritlačíme, aby držali. Praclík preložíme na pripravený plech a voľne prikryjeme čistým igelitovým vrecom. Opakujeme so zvyšnými valčekmi a praclíky rozložíme na plechu rovnomerne od seba.
8. Voľne prikrytý plech dáme do chladničky aspoň na 2 hodiny a najviac na 24 hodín.

9. Rošt nastavíme do stredu rúry a rúru rozohrejeme na 205 °C (teplovzdušnú na 185 °C). Kým sa rúra zohrieva, z plechu s praclíkmi odstránime vrece a praclíky necháme v chladničke odkryté aspoň 30 minút (a najviac hodinu).

10. Máčanie praclíkov: ak používame lúhový kúpeľ, do plechu s okrajom vystlaného papierom na pečenie vložíme mriežku a vystriekame ju sprejom proti prilepeniu. Druhý plech vystelieme papierom na pečenie a položíme ho vedľa prvého. Do veľkej nereaktívnej nádoby (napríklad z varného skla, skla alebo nehrdzavejúcej ocele, misy alebo zapekacej misy) nalejeme vodu. Nádobu postavíme do stredu druhého plechu. V rukaviciach a ochranných okuliaroch posypeme hladinu vody lúhom a necháme ho rozpustiť, asi 5 minút. (Je veľmi dôležité najprv naliať do nádoby celé množstvo vody a až potom pridať lúh; ak by sme dali lúh do nádoby a vodu naliali naň, mohli by sme vyvolať prudkú reakciu.) Kým sa rúra zohrieva, nádobu voľne prikryjeme papierom na pečenie.

11. V rukaviciach a ochranných okuliaroch preložíme jeden praclík do lúhového kúpeľa spodnou stranou nahor a necháme ho v ňom 30 až 40 sekúnd. (Ak treba, praclík jemne pridržíme pod hladinou nereaktívnou lyžicou.) Rukami v rukaviciach preložíme praclík lícom nahor na mriežku odkvapkať. Opakujeme so zvyšnými praclíkmi. Keď sú všetky praclíky namočené, preložíme ich späť na pôvodný plech s okrajom lícom nahor a rovnomerne od seba. Praclíky rovnomerne posypeme praclíkovou soľou a vložíme do rúry. Pečieme dotmavohneda, 12 až 14 minút. (Praclíky namáčané v lúhu budú prirodzene tmavšie než tie namáčané v sóde bikarbóne.) Praclíky zľahka postriekame vodou z rozprašovača a vrátime do rúry, kým nie sú lesklé, 30 sekúnd.
12. Praclíky vyberieme z rúry a pred podávaním ich necháme 5 minút chladnúť.

2. Platňu na pečenie zohrejeme na strednom ohni. en.v: To bake the croissants the next day, after the first 2- to 2 1/2-hour proof, brush them lightly with the beaten egg, wrap them in plastic wrap and refrigerate. The next morning, let them sit at room temperature for 30 to 40 minutes, then heat the oven, brush them again with egg and bake as directed. They taste best the day they are baked; they keep in an airtight container at room temperature overnight and can be refreshed in a 150 °C oven for 5 to 8 minutes.

Ráno ich nechajte 30 až 40 minút pri izbovej teplote, potom rozohrejte rúru, znova ich potrite vajcom a pečte podľa receptu. Najlepšie chutia v deň upečenia; vo vzduchotesnej nádobe vydržia pri izbovej teplote do rána a osviežiť ich môžete v rúre pri 150 °C 5 až 8 minút.

en.t: 265 ml milk, at room temperature
1 package (2 1/2 tsp (7.5 g)) active dry yeast or 19 g fresh cake yeast
270 g unbleached all-purpose flour
80 g bread flour
2 tsp (6 g) kosher salt
50 g sugar
2 tbsp (28 g) unsalted butter, very soft, plus 225 g cold unsalted butter
1 egg (≈50 g without shell)

sk.t: 1 vrecko (2 ½ ČL (7,5 g)) aktívneho sušeného droždia alebo 19 g čerstvého droždia
2 tbsp (28 g) unsalted butter, very soft, plus 225 g cold unsalted butter

en.t: 1. Using a stand mixer fitted with the dough hook (or a hand mixer), mix together the milk and yeast on low speed for 5 to 10 seconds to dissolve the yeast. Add the all-purpose flour, bread flour, salt, sugar, and the 2 tbsp (30 ml) soft butter and continue to mix on low speed for 3 to 4 minutes, or until the butter is fully incorporated and the dough is smooth. Remove the dough from the mixer bowl, place it on a tray, and cover it loosely with plastic wrap. This dough block is called the détrempe. Place the tray in the refrigerator for at least 6 hours or for up to 12 hours. The dough will firm up and the yeast will take some action and proof a bit.

2. At least 6 hours later, put the détrempe on a well-floured work surface, and then press down firmly to create about a 20 cm square. Rotate the square so that, as you face it, it looks like a baseball diamond. Use the sides of your palm to mark a 15 cm square in the middle of the diamond, creating triangular flaps at the 4 corners.

3. As best you can, roll out each of the triangular flaps into a squarish shape (about 7.5 cm squares). You will have to tug a bit at the edges to pull the flap into a square as you roll. When you are done, the entire piece of dough will be about 30 cm wide and tall, with a 15 cm-square lump in the middle and one squarish flap off of each side of that lump. The 15 cm-square lump will be about 2.5 cm thick, and the 4 squarish flaps will be about 0.5 cm thick.

4. Place the 225 g cold butter in the stand mixer fitted with the paddle attachment, and beat on medium speed for 15 to 20 seconds to break up the butter, yet still keep it quite cold. (Alternatively, pound the cold butter with a rolling pin to soften it and shape it into a 15 cm square.) Scrape the butter out of the bowl directly onto the 15 cm-square lump in the center of the dough, and pat it with your fingers into a square that covers the 15 cm-square lump. The butter should be about the same consistency as the dough.

5. Fold one of the flaps up and stretch it over the butter square to cover it entirely. (The dough is quite stretchy, so you can stretch it to cover the butter completely.) Fold and stretch a second flap over the first flap, then repeat with the third and then the fourth flap. Tug at the flaps to keep them in a square that covers the butter. You will now have a butter square that is entirely encased in dough above and below. Using the palms of both hands, firmly press down on this dough package to create about a 20 cm square.

6. When the dough package is relatively flat, switch to a rolling pin and continue to flatten the dough by pressing up and down on the package with the pin. Roll out the dough into a rectangle about 41 × 25 cm. As you work, flour the dough and the work surface as needed to prevent the rolling pin from sticking to the dough.

7. Position the rectangle so a long side is facing you. Using a bench scraper or a knife, score the rectangle in half vertically, to create two 25 × 20 cm rectangles. Brush any loose flour off the dough. Lift the right side of the dough and fold it in, so the right edge meets the scored line in the center. Then lift the left side of the dough and fold it in, so the left edge also meets the scored line in the center and meets the right edge, as well. Square off the folds as much as possible so the edges meet neatly, then fold the right half of the dough on top of the left half. This is called a book fold. Your dough will now be 10 cm wide, 25 cm from top to bottom, and about 5 cm thick. Rotate the dough pile clockwise 90°; it will now be 25 cm wide and 10 cm from top to bottom. The process of folding and rotating is called “turning the dough.”

8. Now, roll out the dough into a rectangle about 46 cm wide and 20 cm from top to bottom. The dough might be a little sticky, so, again, be sure to flour the dough and the work surface as needed to prevent the pin from sticking. Using the bench scraper or knife, this time lightly score the rectangle vertically into thirds. Each third will be 15 cm wide and 20 cm from top to bottom. Brush any loose flour off the dough. Take the right third of the dough and flip it over onto the middle third. Then take the left third of the dough and flip that third on top of the middle and right thirds. (This is like folding a business letter.) Your dough should now be about 15 cm wide, 20 cm from top to bottom, and about 5 cm thick. Rotate the dough pile clockwise 90°; it will now be 20 cm wide and 15 cm from top to bottom.

9. Place the dough on a baking sheet and cover it completely with plastic wrap, tucking the plastic under the dough as if you are tucking it into bed. Refrigerate for at least 1 1/2 hours and no more than 3 hours.

10. Remove the dough from the refrigerator and place it on a well-floured work surface, with a long side of the rectangle facing you. This time roll out the dough into a rectangle about 46 cm wide and 30 cm from top to bottom. If the dough resists rolling, let it sit and relax for up to 15 minutes and roll again. Once again score it vertically into thirds, and then give it another letter fold (fold the right third onto the middle third, and fold the left third on top of that). Return the dough to the baking sheet and again cover it completely with plastic wrap. This time let it rest in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours or up to 16 hours.

11. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Remove the dough from the refrigerator, and place it once again on a well-floured work surface, with a long side of the rectangle facing you. Roll it out into a long, narrow rectangle about 76 cm wide and 15–18 cm from top to bottom.

12. Starting at the bottom left corner of the rectangle, make a mark along the bottom edge of the rectangle every 13 cm until you reach the bottom right corner. Then, starting at the top left corner of the rectangle, mark along the top edge exactly midway between the notches on the bottom edge. Your first notch will be 6.5 cm from the left corner and then continue to notch every 13 cm. Use a chef’s knife to cut the dough rectangle into triangles by cutting on the diagonal from notch to notch. You will end up with 10 triangles and a few edge pieces of scrap.

13. Starting at the edge, cut a 2.5 cm vertical slit at the center of the base of each triangle. Turn all of the triangles so the base is at the top, farthest from you, and the point is directed toward you. Pick up a triangle and hold it by its base with one hand and gently stretch it and stroke it lengthwise with your other hand to elongate it to 25–30 cm in length.

14. Place the lengthened triangle on the work surface. Fan open the base at the 2.5 cm slit into a Y, and then roll the dough down to the point. Place the rolled triangle, point-side down, on the parchment-lined baking sheet, so the point is touching the parchment. Repeat with the remaining dough triangles, spacing the pastries 5–7.5 cm apart on the baking sheet.
15. Cover the croissants lightly with plastic wrap and leave them in a warm place for 2 to 2 1/2 hours, or until they are somewhat poufy and airy.
16. In a small bowl, whisk the egg until blended. Gently brush the croissants lightly with the egg.

17. If you are baking the croissants the same day, cover them again with plastic wrap and let them finish proofing for another 1 to 1 1/2 hours. They will get even more poufy and jiggly when you nudge them. (To bake them the next day, see Storage above.)

18. Position a rack in the center of the oven, and heat the oven to 205 °C (fan 185 °C). When the croissants are done proofing, brush them again with the beaten egg. Bake for 5 minutes, then turn down the oven to 175 °C (fan 155 °C) and bake for another 25 to 35 minutes (for a total baking time of 30 to 40 minutes), or until they are golden brown all over. Let cool on the pan on a wire rack for 30 to 40 minutes. Serve warm.

c.t: 1. Using a stand mixer fitted with the dough hook (or a hand mixer), mix together the milk and yeast on low speed for 5 to 10 seconds to dissolve the yeast. Add the all-purpose flour, bread flour, salt, sugar, and the 2 tbsp (30 ml) soft butter and continue to mix on low speed for 3 to 4 minutes, or until the butter is fully incorporated and the dough is smooth. Remove the dough from the mixer bowl, place it on a tray, and cover it loosely with plastic wrap. This dough block is called the détrempe. Place the tray in the refrigerator for at least 6 hours or for up to 12 hours. The dough will firm up and the yeast will take some action and proof a bit.

2. At least 6 hours later, put the détrempe on a well-floured work surface, and then press down firmly to create about a 20 cm square. Rotate the square so that, as you face it, it looks like a baseball diamond. Use the sides of your palm to mark a 15 cm square in the middle of the diamond, creating triangular flaps at the 4 corners.

3. As best you can, roll out each of the triangular flaps into a squarish shape (about 7.5 cm squares). You will have to tug a bit at the edges to pull the flap into a square as you roll. When you are done, the entire piece of dough will be about 30 cm wide and tall, with a 15 cm-square lump in the middle and one squarish flap off of each side of that lump. The 15 cm-square lump will be about 2.5 cm thick, and the 4 squarish flaps will be about 0.5 cm thick.

4. Place the 225 g cold butter in the stand mixer fitted with the paddle attachment, and beat on medium speed for 15 to 20 seconds to break up the butter, yet still keep it quite cold. (Alternatively, pound the cold butter with a rolling pin to soften it and shape it into a 15 cm square.) Scrape the butter out of the bowl directly onto the 15 cm-square lump in the center of the dough, and pat it with your fingers into a square that covers the 15 cm-square lump. The butter should be about the same consistency as the dough.

5. Fold one of the flaps up and stretch it over the butter square to cover it entirely. (The dough is quite stretchy, so you can stretch it to cover the butter completely.) Fold and stretch a second flap over the first flap, then repeat with the third and then the fourth flap. Tug at the flaps to keep them in a square that covers the butter. You will now have a butter square that is entirely encased in dough above and below. Using the palms of both hands, firmly press down on this dough package to create about a 20 cm square.

6. When the dough package is relatively flat, switch to a rolling pin and continue to flatten the dough by pressing up and down on the package with the pin. Roll out the dough into a rectangle about 41 × 25 cm. As you work, flour the dough and the work surface as needed to prevent the rolling pin from sticking to the dough.

7. Position the rectangle so a long side is facing you. Using a bench scraper or a knife, score the rectangle in half vertically, to create two 25 × 20 cm rectangles. Brush any loose flour off the dough. Lift the right side of the dough and fold it in, so the right edge meets the scored line in the center. Then lift the left side of the dough and fold it in, so the left edge also meets the scored line in the center and meets the right edge, as well. Square off the folds as much as possible so the edges meet neatly, then fold the right half of the dough on top of the left half. This is called a book fold. Your dough will now be 10 cm wide, 25 cm from top to bottom, and about 5 cm thick. Rotate the dough pile clockwise 90°; it will now be 25 cm wide and 10 cm from top to bottom. The process of folding and rotating is called “turning the dough.”

8. Now, roll out the dough into a rectangle about 46 cm wide and 20 cm from top to bottom. The dough might be a little sticky, so, again, be sure to flour the dough and the work surface as needed to prevent the pin from sticking. Using the bench scraper or knife, this time lightly score the rectangle vertically into thirds. Each third will be 15 cm wide and 20 cm from top to bottom. Brush any loose flour off the dough. Take the right third of the dough and flip it over onto the middle third. Then take the left third of the dough and flip that third on top of the middle and right thirds. (This is like folding a business letter.) Your dough should now be about 15 cm wide, 20 cm from top to bottom, and about 5 cm thick. Rotate the dough pile clockwise 90°; it will now be 20 cm wide and 15 cm from top to bottom.

9. Place the dough on a baking sheet and cover it completely with plastic wrap, tucking the plastic under the dough as if you are tucking it into bed. Refrigerate for at least 1 1/2 hours and no more than 3 hours.

10. Remove the dough from the refrigerator and place it on a well-floured work surface, with a long side of the rectangle facing you. This time roll out the dough into a rectangle about 46 cm wide and 30 cm from top to bottom. If the dough resists rolling, let it sit and relax for up to 15 minutes and roll again. Once again score it vertically into thirds, and then give it another letter fold (fold the right third onto the middle third, and fold the left third on top of that). Return the dough to the baking sheet and again cover it completely with plastic wrap. This time let it rest in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours or up to 16 hours.

11. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Remove the dough from the refrigerator, and place it once again on a well-floured work surface, with a long side of the rectangle facing you. Roll it out into a long, narrow rectangle about 76 cm wide and 15–18 cm from top to bottom.

12. Starting at the bottom left corner of the rectangle, make a mark along the bottom edge of the rectangle every 13 cm until you reach the bottom right corner. Then, starting at the top left corner of the rectangle, mark along the top edge exactly midway between the notches on the bottom edge. Your first notch will be 6.5 cm from the left corner and then continue to notch every 13 cm. Use a chef’s knife to cut the dough rectangle into triangles by cutting on the diagonal from notch to notch. You will end up with 10 triangles and a few edge pieces of scrap.

13. Starting at the edge, cut a 2.5 cm vertical slit at the center of the base of each triangle. Turn all of the triangles so the base is at the top, farthest from you, and the point is directed toward you. Pick up a triangle and hold it by its base with one hand and gently stretch it and stroke it lengthwise with your other hand to elongate it to 25–30 cm in length.

14. Place the lengthened triangle on the work surface. Fan open the base at the 2.5 cm slit into a Y, and then roll the dough down to the point. Place the rolled triangle, point-side down, on the parchment-lined baking sheet, so the point is touching the parchment. Repeat with the remaining dough triangles, spacing the pastries 5–7.5 cm apart on the baking sheet.
15. Cover the croissants lightly with plastic wrap and leave them in a warm place for 2 to 2 1/2 hours, or until they are somewhat poufy and airy.
16. In a small bowl, whisk the egg until blended. Gently brush the croissants lightly with the egg.

17. If you are baking the croissants the same day, cover them again with plastic wrap and let them finish proofing for another 1 to 1 1/2 hours. They will get even more poufy and jiggly when you nudge them. (To bake them the next day, see Storage above.)

18. Position a rack in the center of the oven, and heat the oven to 205 °C (fan 185 °C). When the croissants are done proofing, brush them again with the beaten egg. Bake for 5 minutes, then turn down the oven to 175 °C (fan 155 °C) and bake for another 25 to 35 minutes (for a total baking time of 30 to 40 minutes), or until they are golden brown all over. Let cool on the pan on a wire rack for 30 to 40 minutes. Serve warm.

1. V stojanovom mixéri s hákom na cesto (alebo ručným mixérom) miešame mlieko a droždie na nízkej rýchlosti 5 až 10 sekúnd, aby sa droždie rozpustilo. Pridáme hladkú múku, chlebovú múku, soľ, cukor a 2 PL (30 ml) mäkkého masla a miešame na nízkej rýchlosti ďalšie 3 až 4 minúty, kým sa maslo úplne nezapracuje a cesto nie je hladké. Cesto vyberieme z misy mixéra, položíme na tácku a voľne prikryjeme potravinovou fóliou. Tento blok cesta sa nazýva détrempe. Tácku dáme do chladničky aspoň na 6 hodín alebo najviac na 12 hodín. Cesto stuhne a droždie začne pracovať a cesto trochu nakysne.

2. Najskôr o 6 hodín položíme détrempe na dobre pomúčenú pracovnú plochu a pevne ho stlačíme na štvorec so stranou asi 20 cm. Štvorec otočíme tak, aby pred nami vyzeral ako kosoštvorec. Hranou dlane vyznačíme v strede kosoštvorca štvorec so stranou 15 cm, čím v 4 rohoch vzniknú trojuholníkové cípy.

3. Každý trojuholníkový cíp čo najlepšie vyvaľkáme do približne štvorcového tvaru (štvorce so stranou asi 7,5 cm). Pri vaľkaní budeme musieť okraje trochu potiahnuť, aby z cípu vznikol štvorec. Keď skončíme, celý kus cesta bude mať na šírku aj na výšku asi 30 cm, so štvorcovou hrčou so stranou 15 cm v strede a jedným približne štvorcovým cípom na každej jej strane. Štvorcová hrča so stranou 15 cm bude hrubá asi 2,5 cm a 4 približne štvorcové cípy asi 0,5 cm.

4. Vložíme 225 g studeného masla do stojanového mixéra s plochým miešadlom a na strednej rýchlosti ho šľaháme 15 až 20 sekúnd, aby sa rozbilo, no zostalo dosť studené. (Studené maslo môžeme aj zmäkčiť údermi valčeka a vytvarovať ho do štvorca so stranou 15 cm.) Maslo zoškrabeme z misy priamo na štvorcovú hrču so stranou 15 cm v strede cesta a prstami ho uklepeme do štvorca, ktorý túto hrču so stranou 15 cm prekryje. Maslo by malo mať približne rovnakú konzistenciu ako cesto.

5. Jeden cíp preložíme nahor a natiahneme ho cez štvorec masla tak, aby ho celý prikryl. (Cesto je dosť pružné, takže ho môžeme natiahnuť a maslo úplne zakryť.) Druhý cíp preložíme a natiahneme cez prvý a to isté zopakujeme s tretím a štvrtým cípom. Cípy poťahujeme tak, aby tvorili štvorec, ktorý maslo zakrýva. Teraz máme štvorec masla celý obalený cestom zhora aj zdola. Oboma dlaňami tento balíček cesta pevne stlačíme na štvorec so stranou asi 20 cm.

6. Keď je balíček pomerne plochý, prejdeme na valček a cesto ďalej splošťujeme pritláčaním valčeka zhora nadol. Cesto vyvaľkáme na obdĺžnik s rozmermi asi 41 × 25 cm. Počas práce cesto aj pracovnú plochu podľa potreby pomúčime, aby sa valček neprilepil k cestu.

7. Obdĺžnik otočíme dlhšou stranou k sebe. Škrabkou alebo nožom ho zvislo narežeme na polovicu, čím vzniknú dva obdĺžniky s rozmermi 25 × 20 cm. Z cesta zmetieme voľnú múku. Pravú stranu cesta zdvihneme a preložíme dovnútra tak, aby sa pravý okraj stretol s vyznačenou čiarou v strede. Potom zdvihneme ľavú stranu a preložíme ju dovnútra tak, aby sa ľavý okraj tiež stretol s čiarou v strede a s pravým okrajom. Prehyby čo najviac zarovnáme, aby sa okraje úhľadne stretli, a potom pravú polovicu cesta preložíme na ľavú. Toto sa nazýva knižné prekladanie. Cesto bude teraz široké 10 cm, zhora nadol 25 cm a hrubé asi 5 cm. Kôpku cesta otočíme v smere hodinových ručičiek o 90°; teraz bude široká 25 cm a zhora nadol 10 cm. Tento postup prekladania a otáčania sa nazýva „prekladanie cesta“.

8. Teraz cesto vyvaľkáme na obdĺžnik široký asi 46 cm a zhora nadol 20 cm. Cesto môže byť trochu lepkavé, takže opäť podľa potreby pomúčime cesto aj pracovnú plochu, aby sa valček neprilepil. Škrabkou alebo nožom tentoraz obdĺžnik zľahka zvislo narežeme na tretiny. Každá tretina bude široká 15 cm a zhora nadol 20 cm. Z cesta zmetieme voľnú múku. Pravú tretinu cesta preklopíme na strednú tretinu. Potom ľavú tretinu preklopíme na strednú a pravú tretinu. (Je to ako skladanie listu do obálky.) Cesto by teraz malo byť široké asi 15 cm, zhora nadol 20 cm a hrubé asi 5 cm. Kôpku cesta otočíme v smere hodinových ručičiek o 90°; teraz bude široká 20 cm a zhora nadol 15 cm.
9. Cesto položíme na plech a celé ho prikryjeme potravinovou fóliou, ktorú zastrčíme pod cesto, akoby sme ho ukladali do postele. Dáme do chladničky aspoň na 1 1/2 hodiny a najviac na 3 hodiny.

10. Cesto vyberieme z chladničky a položíme na dobre pomúčenú pracovnú plochu dlhšou stranou obdĺžnika k sebe. Tentoraz ho vyvaľkáme na obdĺžnik široký asi 46 cm a zhora nadol 30 cm. Ak sa cesto vaľkaniu bráni, necháme ho najviac 15 minút odpočinúť a vaľkáme znova. Opäť ho zvislo narežeme na tretiny a znova preložíme ako list (pravú tretinu na strednú a ľavú tretinu navrch). Cesto vrátime na plech a opäť ho celé prikryjeme potravinovou fóliou. Tentoraz ho necháme v chladničke odpočívať aspoň 4 hodiny alebo najviac 16 hodín.

11. Plech vystelieme papierom na pečenie. Cesto vyberieme z chladničky a znova ho položíme na dobre pomúčenú pracovnú plochu dlhšou stranou obdĺžnika k sebe. Vyvaľkáme ho na dlhý úzky obdĺžnik široký asi 76 cm a zhora nadol 15–18 cm.

12. Od ľavého dolného rohu obdĺžnika urobíme pozdĺž spodného okraja značku každých 13 cm, až kým nedosiahneme pravý dolný roh. Potom od ľavého horného rohu značíme pozdĺž horného okraja presne v polovici medzi zárezmi na spodnom okraji. Prvý zárez bude 6,5 cm od ľavého rohu a potom pokračujeme so zárezom každých 13 cm. Kuchárskym nožom rozrežeme obdĺžnik cesta na trojuholníky šikmými rezmi od zárezu k zárezu. Dostaneme 10 trojuholníkov a niekoľko okrajových zvyškov.

13. Od okraja urobíme v strede základne každého trojuholníka zvislý zárez dlhý 2,5 cm. Všetky trojuholníky otočíme tak, aby základňa bola hore, najďalej od nás, a špička smerovala k nám. Zdvihneme trojuholník, jednou rukou ho držíme za základňu a druhou ho jemne naťahujeme a hladíme po dĺžke, aby sme ho predĺžili na 25–30 cm.

14. Predĺžený trojuholník položíme na pracovnú plochu. Základňu pri záreze dlhom 2,5 cm roztvoríme do tvaru Y a cesto zvinieme až ku špičke. Zvinutý trojuholník položíme špičkou nadol na plech vystlaný papierom na pečenie tak, aby sa špička dotýkala papiera. Opakujeme so zvyšnými trojuholníkmi a pečivo rozložíme na plechu 5–7,5 cm od seba.
15. Croissanty zľahka prikryjeme potravinovou fóliou a necháme ich na teplom mieste 2 až 2 1/2 hodiny, kým nie sú pomerne nadýchané a vzdušné.
16. V malej miske metličkou rozšľaháme vajce. Croissanty ním jemne a zľahka potrieme.

17. Ak croissanty pečieme v ten istý deň, znova ich prikryjeme fóliou a necháme ich dokysnúť ešte 1 až 1 1/2 hodiny. Budú ešte nadýchanejšie a pri dotyku sa budú chvieť. (Ak ich chceme piecť až na druhý deň, pozri Skladovanie vyššie.)

18. Rošt nastavíme do stredu rúry a rúru rozohrejeme na 205 °C (teplovzdušnú na 185 °C). Keď croissanty dokysnú, znova ich potrieme rozšľahaným vajcom. Pečieme 5 minút, potom rúru stiahneme na 175 °C (teplovzdušnú na 155 °C) a pečieme ďalších 25 až 35 minút (celkový čas pečenia 30 až 40 minút), kým nie sú celé zlatistohnedé. Necháme chladnúť na plechu na mriežke 30 až 40 minút. Podávame teplé.

en.v: Store any leftover rolls, well wrapped, at room temperature for several days; freeze for longer storage.

sk.v: Zvyšné rožky uchovávame dobre zabalené pri izbovej teplote niekoľko dní; na dlhšie skladovanie ich zmrazíme.

en.t: 340 g water, milk or a combination
50 g granulated sugar
540 g King Arthur Unbleached All-Purpose Flour
2 1/2 tsp (7.5 g) instant yeast
2 1/2 tsp (15 g) table salt
4 tbsp (57 g) unsalted butter, softened
24 tbsp (340 g) unsalted butter, cold
16 to 32 (85 g to 170 g) Pain au Chocolat Sticks, (depending on whether you want one or two sticks inside each roll)
1 large egg (≈50 g without shell), beaten with a pinch of salt

sk.t: 340 g water, milk or a combination
16–32 čokoládových tyčiniek do pain au chocolat (85–170 g), podľa toho, či chcete do každej rolky jednu alebo dve
1 veľké vajce (≈50 g bez škrupiny), rozšľahané so štipkou soli

en.t: 1. To make the dough: In a large mixing bowl, stir together the water, sugar, 240 g of the flour, yeast, salt, and butter. Mix until fairly evenly blended.

2. Add the remaining flour and stir until the dough pulls away from the side of the bowl. Turn the dough out and knead it until it just starts to smooth out. You don't want to over-knead it at this point, since it's going to spend a considerable amount of time rising.

3. Place the dough in a lightly greased bowl, cover, and let rise for about an hour, until puffy. (The dough can be prepared to this point in a bread machine with at least a 680 g capacity. Simply place all of the ingredients in the bucket, select dough or manual, and press start.)
4. After an hour at room temperature, refrigerate the dough (in its covered bowl) for 8 to 16 hours; overnight is your best bet.

5. To prepare the butter: Just before the dough is ready to come out of the fridge, prepare the butter for rolling into the dough. Cut each of the three sticks in half lengthwise and place all six pieces on a floured piece of waxed paper or plastic wrap. Sprinkle flour on the top surface of the butter, cover with another piece of paper or plastic and gently pound it with a rolling pin until it becomes malleable. Then roll the butter out until it's about 20 × 20 cm.

6. To assemble the rolls: Remove the dough from the refrigerator, place it on a lightly floured surface and roll it into a 30 cm square. Place the butter in the center of the dough at a 45° angle; it'll look like a diamond inside the square. Fold the four flaps of dough into the center to enclose the butter, pinching them together as best you can.
7. Roll the dough into a 25 × 51 cm rectangle. Fold one third into the center, then the opposite third over the first, like you were folding a business letter; this is called a letter fold.
8. Turn the dough 90° and roll it into a 25 × 51 cm rectangle again.

9. Fold each of the shorter edges toward the center until they meet without overlapping. Fold the dough in half along the center where the edges meet, as if closing a book, then turn it 90°; this is called a book fold.
10. Wrap the dough in lightly floured plastic wrap and refrigerate it again for at least 8 hours (or up to 24 hours), until you're ready to use it.
11. To finish your pain au chocolat: Remove the dough from the refrigerator, cut it in half and return one half to the refrigerator.
12. Roll the other half out until it's a generous 20 × 61 cm. With a bench knife, cut the dough into eight 10 × 15 cm pieces.

13. Place one or two pieces of chocolate at one end of each piece and roll it up into a tube. Place, seam side down, on a lightly greased or parchment lined baking sheet. Press down on the tops of the rolls to flatten them into a rectangle shape. Repeat with the remaining dough. Cover and let rise in a warm place until they're light and puffy looking, about an hour.
14. Towards the end of the rising time, preheat the oven to 220 °C (fan 200 °C).

c.t: 1. To make the dough: In a large mixing bowl, stir together the water, sugar, 240 g of the flour, yeast, salt, and butter. Mix until fairly evenly blended.

2. Add the remaining flour and stir until the dough pulls away from the side of the bowl. Turn the dough out and knead it until it just starts to smooth out. You don't want to over-knead it at this point, since it's going to spend a considerable amount of time rising.

3. Place the dough in a lightly greased bowl, cover, and let rise for about an hour, until puffy. (The dough can be prepared to this point in a bread machine with at least a 680 g capacity. Simply place all of the ingredients in the bucket, select dough or manual, and press start.)
4. After an hour at room temperature, refrigerate the dough (in its covered bowl) for 8 to 16 hours; overnight is your best bet.

5. To prepare the butter: Just before the dough is ready to come out of the fridge, prepare the butter for rolling into the dough. Cut each of the three sticks in half lengthwise and place all six pieces on a floured piece of waxed paper or plastic wrap. Sprinkle flour on the top surface of the butter, cover with another piece of paper or plastic and gently pound it with a rolling pin until it becomes malleable. Then roll the butter out until it's about 20 × 20 cm.

6. To assemble the rolls: Remove the dough from the refrigerator, place it on a lightly floured surface and roll it into a 30 cm square. Place the butter in the center of the dough at a 45° angle; it'll look like a diamond inside the square. Fold the four flaps of dough into the center to enclose the butter, pinching them together as best you can.
7. Roll the dough into a 25 × 51 cm rectangle. Fold one third into the center, then the opposite third over the first, like you were folding a business letter; this is called a letter fold.
8. Turn the dough 90° and roll it into a 25 × 51 cm rectangle again.

9. Fold each of the shorter edges toward the center until they meet without overlapping. Fold the dough in half along the center where the edges meet, as if closing a book, then turn it 90°; this is called a book fold.
10. Wrap the dough in lightly floured plastic wrap and refrigerate it again for at least 8 hours (or up to 24 hours), until you're ready to use it.
11. To finish your pain au chocolat: Remove the dough from the refrigerator, cut it in half and return one half to the refrigerator.
12. Roll the other half out until it's a generous 20 × 61 cm. With a bench knife, cut the dough into eight 10 × 15 cm pieces.

13. Place one or two pieces of chocolate at one end of each piece and roll it up into a tube. Place, seam side down, on a lightly greased or parchment lined baking sheet. Press down on the tops of the rolls to flatten them into a rectangle shape. Repeat with the remaining dough. Cover and let rise in a warm place until they're light and puffy looking, about an hour.
14. Towards the end of the rising time, preheat the oven to 220 °C (fan 200 °C).

15. Just before baking, brush the egg/salt glaze over the tops of the rolls. Bake the rolls for 18 to 20 minutes, until golden brown. Remove them from the oven and allow them to cool a bit before you bite into them; the structure needs a chance to set.
16. Storage information: Store any leftover rolls, well wrapped, at room temperature for several days; freeze for longer storage.
1. Príprava cesta: vo veľkej mise zmiešame vodu, cukor, 240 g múky, droždie, soľ a maslo. Miešame, kým sa pomerne rovnomerne nespoja.
2. Pridáme zvyšnú múku a miešame, kým sa cesto neodlepí od stien misy. Cesto vyklopíme a miesime, len kým nezačne byť hladké. V tejto fáze ho nechceme premiesiť, keďže bude ešte dlho kysnúť.

3. Cesto vložíme do zľahka vymastenej misy, prikryjeme a necháme kysnúť asi hodinu, kým nie je nadýchané. (Cesto môžeme do tejto fázy pripraviť aj v domácej pekárni s kapacitou aspoň 680 g. Všetky suroviny jednoducho vložíme do nádoby, zvolíme program na cesto alebo manuálny režim a spustíme.)
4. Po hodine pri izbovej teplote dáme cesto (v prikrytej mise) do chladničky na 8 až 16 hodín; najlepšie cez noc.

5. Príprava masla: tesne predtým, ako je cesto pripravené na vybratie z chladničky, pripravíme maslo na zavaľkanie do cesta. Každú z troch tyčiniek masla rozrežeme pozdĺžne na polovicu a všetkých šesť kúskov položíme na pomúčený kus voskovaného papiera alebo potravinovej fólie. Vrch masla posypeme múkou, prikryjeme ďalším kusom papiera alebo fólie a jemne ho vyklepeme valčekom, kým nie je poddajné. Potom maslo vyvaľkáme asi na 20 × 20 cm.

6. Zostavenie: cesto vyberieme z chladničky, položíme na zľahka pomúčenú plochu a vyvaľkáme na štvorec so stranou 30 cm. Maslo položíme do stredu cesta pod uhlom 45°; bude vyzerať ako kosoštvorec vnútri štvorca. Štyri cípy cesta preložíme do stredu, aby maslo uzavreli, a čo najlepšie ich spojíme.
7. Cesto vyvaľkáme na obdĺžnik s rozmermi 25 × 51 cm. Jednu tretinu preložíme do stredu a potom protiľahlú tretinu cez prvú, ako keď skladáme list do obálky; toto sa nazýva jednoduché prekladanie.
8. Cesto otočíme o 90° a znova ho vyvaľkáme na obdĺžnik s rozmermi 25 × 51 cm.

9. Oba kratšie okraje preložíme do stredu, kým sa nestretnú bez prekrytia. Cesto preložíme na polovicu v strede, kde sa okraje stretávajú, akoby sme zatvárali knihu, a potom ho otočíme o 90°; toto sa nazýva knižné prekladanie.
10. Cesto zabalíme do zľahka pomúčenej potravinovej fólie a znova ho dáme do chladničky aspoň na 8 hodín (alebo najviac na 24 hodín), kým ho nepoužijeme.
11. Dokončenie pain au chocolat: cesto vyberieme z chladničky, rozrežeme na polovicu a jednu polovicu vrátime do chladničky.
12. Druhú polovicu vyvaľkáme na obdĺžnik s rozmermi aspoň 20 × 61 cm. Škrabkou ho rozrežeme na osem kúskov s rozmermi 10 × 15 cm.

13. Na jeden koniec každého kúska položíme jeden alebo dva kúsky čokolády a zvinieme ho do rolky. Uložíme spojom nadol na zľahka vymastený alebo papierom vystlaný plech. Vrch rolky stlačíme, aby sme ju sploštili do obdĺžnikového tvaru. Opakujeme so zvyšným cestom. Prikryjeme a necháme kysnúť na teplom mieste, kým nie sú ľahké a nadýchané, asi hodinu.
14. Ku koncu kysnutia rozohrejeme rúru na 220 °C (teplovzdušnú na 200 °C).

15. Tesne pred pečením potrieme vrch rolky vaječno-soľnou glazúrou. Pečieme 18 až 20 minút do zlatistohneda. Vyberieme z rúry a pred zahryznutím ich necháme trochu vychladnúť; štruktúra sa potrebuje ustáliť.
16. Skladovanie: zvyšné pečivo dobre zabalené uchovávame pri izbovej teplote niekoľko dní; na dlhšie skladovanie ho zamrazíme.

en.t: 1. Begin by cutting a 0.5 cm slice off the end of each of the four 113 g sticks in the 450 g pack; you'll have about 2 tbsp (28 g) butter. Set them (and the remaining butter) aside. You'll be using the 2 tbsp (28 g) butter immediately, but won't need the remaining butter until after you've made the dough.

2. In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, yeast, salt, and cardamom. Add the 2 tbsp (28 g) cold butter, working it in with your fingers until no large lumps remain. This step coats the flour a bit with fat, making the pastry a tiny bit more tender.

3. Add the vanilla, milk, water, and eggs. Mix and knead to make a cohesive, but quite sticky dough. This is easily done in a bread machine set on the dough cycle; or in a mixer. If you use a mixer, the dough won't completely clean the bowl; it'll probably leave a narrow ring around the side, and stick at the bottom.
4. Scrape the dough into a ball, and transfer it to a floured work surface. Cover it with plastic wrap, and let it rest for 10 minutes while you prepare the butter.

5. Cut each 113 g piece of butter in half lengthwise, to make 8 long rectangles. On a piece of floured parchment or plastic wrap, line up 4 of the butter pieces side by side, to form a rectangle. Sprinkle lightly with flour, and cover with another piece of parchment or plastic wrap.

6. Gently pound and roll the butter until it's about 15 × 23 cm. The pieces may or may not meld together. If they do, great, they'll be easier to work with. If not, though, that's OK; don't stress about it.
7. Repeat with the remaining 4 pieces of butter. You should now have two butter rectangles, about 15 × 23 cm each.
8. Roll the dough into a rectangle about 30 cm wide and 61 cm long. Don't worry about being ultra-precise; this is just a guide, though you should try to get fairly close.

9. Place one of the butter pieces onto the center third of the dough. Fold one side over the butter to cover it. Place the other butter piece atop the folded-over dough, and fold the remaining dough up over it. You now have a rectangular "packet" of dough-enclosed butter. Pinch the open ends and side closed as best you can.

10. Turn the dough 90°, so a 30 cm side is closest to you. Roll the dough into a 25 × 61 cm rectangle (approximately). Fold each side into the center; then fold one side over the other to make a rectangular packet about 15 × 25 cm.
11. Dust the surface of the dough with flour, wrap it in plastic wrap, and chill in the refrigerator for about 20 minutes.

12. Remove the dough from the fridge, and again roll it into a rectangle about 25 × 61 cm. Fold it into a packet as you did in step #10; it'll be about 18 × 30 cm. Roll one final time, fold into a packet, and flour the dough lightly. Wrap loosely (but completely) in plastic, and chill it for 2 hours, or up to 16 hours; we prefer the longer refrigeration, as it gives the dough a chance to relax and rise.

13. Before shaping the pastries, select your filling(s). We like to use a variety. Either of the filling suggestions in this recipe make enough to fill all the pastries; so if you want to mix and match, make a half-recipe of the cheese filling, and use only half the amount of fruit filling called for.
14. To make the cheese filling, combine all of the ingredients, stirring until smooth. For the smoothest filling, process in a food processor.
15. When you're ready to make pastries, remove the dough from the refrigerator, unwrap it, and cut off one-third. You'll work with this piece first; return the remainder to the fridge.

16. Divide the dough into 12 pieces. Roll each into a smooth ball, then flatten the balls into 7.5 cm to 9 cm rounds, making the center thinner than the edges. You want to build up a slight wall of dough all around the circumference; this will help hold the filling. Place the rounds on a parchment-lined or lightly greased baking sheet.
17. Working with one-half of the remaining dough at a time, repeat the process; you'll finish with three baking sheets, each with 12 dough rounds.
18. Cover the Danish lightly with greased plastic wrap, and let them rise for about 1 hour; they'll become slightly puffy. Towards the end of the rising time, preheat the oven to 205 °C (fan 185 °C).
19. Use your fingers to press the centers of the dough rounds as flat as possible, leaving the "sidewalls" puffed. Spoon a slightly heaping teaspoon of filling into the well of each round.
20. Brush the exposed edges of pastry with the egg/water topping; this will create a satiny, golden crust.
21. Bake the pastries for 15 to 18 minutes, until they're golden brown. Remove them from the oven, and transfer to a rack. Glaze and serve immediately; or wait until they cool, then glaze.
22. To make the glaze, whisk the confectioners' sugar and salt with enough water or milk to make a "drizzle-able" glaze.
23. Drizzle the glaze atop the pastries. Sprinkle with crushed nuts.

1. Najprv z konca každej zo štyroch 113 g tyčiniek masla v 450 g balení odrežeme plátok hrubý 0,5 cm; dostaneme asi 2 PL (28 g) masla. Plátky (aj zvyšné maslo) odložíme. 2 PL (28 g) masla použijeme hneď, zvyšné maslo budeme potrebovať až po príprave cesta.

2. Vo veľkej mise metličkou premiešame múku, cukor, droždie, soľ a kardamóm. Pridáme 2 PL (28 g) studeného masla a prstami ho zapracujeme, kým nezostanú veľké hrudky. Týmto krokom sa múka trochu obalí tukom a pečivo bude o niečo jemnejšie.

3. Pridáme vanilku, mlieko, vodu a vajcia. Zmiešame a vypracujeme súdržné, ale dosť lepkavé cesto. Ľahko to zvládneme v domácej pekárni na programe na cesto alebo v mixéri. Ak použijeme mixér, cesto sa od misy úplne neodlepí; pravdepodobne zostane úzky prstenec po stenách a prilepí sa na dne.
4. Cesto zoškrabeme do gule a preložíme na pomúčenú pracovnú plochu. Prikryjeme potravinovou fóliou a necháme 10 minút odpočívať, kým pripravíme maslo.

5. Každý 113 g kus masla rozrežeme pozdĺžne na polovicu, čím vznikne 8 dlhých obdĺžnikov. Na pomúčený papier na pečenie alebo potravinovú fóliu uložíme 4 kúsky masla vedľa seba do obdĺžnika. Zľahka posypeme múkou a prikryjeme ďalším kusom papiera alebo fólie.
6. Maslo jemne vyklepeme a vyvaľkáme asi na 15 × 23 cm. Kúsky sa môžu, ale nemusia spojiť. Ak sa spoja, výborne, bude sa s nimi ľahšie pracovať. Ak nie, nevadí; netrápime sa tým.
7. Opakujeme so zvyšnými 4 kúskami masla. Teraz by sme mali mať dva obdĺžniky masla, každý asi 15 × 23 cm.
8. Cesto vyvaľkáme na obdĺžnik široký asi 30 cm a dlhý 61 cm. S presnosťou si netrápime hlavu; je to len orientačné, no mali by sme sa k tomu dosť priblížiť.

9. Jeden kus masla položíme na strednú tretinu cesta. Jednu stranu cesta preložíme cez maslo, aby ho zakryla. Druhý kus masla položíme na preložené cesto a zvyšné cesto preložíme cezeň. Teraz máme obdĺžnikový „balíček“ masla uzavretého v ceste. Otvorené konce a bok čo najlepšie stlačíme, aby sa uzavreli.

10. Cesto otočíme o 90° tak, aby bola k nám najbližšie strana s dĺžkou 30 cm. Cesto vyvaľkáme na obdĺžnik s rozmermi (približne) 25 × 61 cm. Obe strany preložíme do stredu; potom jednu stranu preložíme cez druhú, čím vznikne obdĺžnikový balíček s rozmermi asi 15 × 25 cm.
11. Povrch cesta poprášime múkou, zabalíme do potravinovej fólie a dáme asi na 20 minút do chladničky.

12. Cesto vyberieme z chladničky a znova ho vyvaľkáme na obdĺžnik s rozmermi asi 25 × 61 cm. Preložíme ho do balíčka ako v kroku 10; bude mať asi 18 × 30 cm. Naposledy ho vyvaľkáme, preložíme do balíčka a cesto zľahka pomúčime. Voľne (ale celé) zabalíme do fólie a necháme v chladničke 2 hodiny alebo najviac 16 hodín; uprednostňujeme dlhšie chladenie, pretože cesto sa tak stihne uvoľniť a nakysnúť.

13. Pred tvarovaním pečiva si vyberieme plnku (plnky). Radi používame rôzne. Ktorákoľvek z navrhovaných plniek v tomto recepte stačí na naplnenie všetkého pečiva; ak ich teda chceme kombinovať, pripravíme polovičnú dávku syrovej plnky a použijeme len polovicu predpísaného množstva ovocnej plnky.
14. Na syrovú plnku zmiešame všetky suroviny a miešame do hladka. Najhladšiu plnku získame v kuchynskom robote.
15. Keď sme pripravení tvarovať pečivo, cesto vyberieme z chladničky, rozbalíme a odrežeme z neho tretinu. Najprv budeme pracovať s týmto kusom; zvyšok vrátime do chladničky.

16. Cesto rozdelíme na 12 kúskov. Každý vyvaľkáme do hladkej guľky a guľky sploštíme na placky s priemerom 7,5 cm až 9 cm, pričom stred bude tenší než okraje. Po celom obvode chceme vytvoriť mierny múrik z cesta; pomôže udržať plnku. Placky uložíme na plech vystlaný papierom na pečenie alebo zľahka vymastený.
17. Postup opakujeme vždy s polovicou zvyšného cesta; nakoniec budeme mať tri plechy, na každom 12 placiek z cesta.
18. Pečivo zľahka prikryjeme vymastenou potravinovou fóliou a necháme kysnúť asi 1 hodinu; trochu nabobtná. Ku koncu kysnutia rozohrejeme rúru na 205 °C (teplovzdušnú na 185 °C).
19. Prstami stlačíme stred placiek čo najviac naplocho a „bočné steny“ necháme nadýchané. Do priehlbiny každej placky dáme vrchovatú lyžičku plnky.
20. Odkryté okraje pečiva potrieme vaječno-vodovou zmesou; vytvorí saténovo lesklú zlatistú kôrku.
21. Pečivo pečieme 15 až 18 minút do zlatistohneda. Vyberieme z rúry a preložíme na mriežku. Polejeme glazúrou a hneď podávame; alebo počkáme, kým vychladne, a polejeme ho potom.
22. Na glazúru metličkou zmiešame práškový cukor a soľ s takým množstvom vody alebo mlieka, aby vznikla glazúra, ktorou sa dá pokvapkať.
23. Pečivo pokvapkáme glazúrou. Posypeme drvenými orechmi.

en.t: 1. Preheat the oven to 205 °C (fan 185 °C). Peel and core the apples, and slice them into 1.5 cm slices. Toss with the 3 tbsp (44 ml) sugar, 1 tbsp (15 ml) flour, a pinch of salt, and the juice of 1/4 lemon.

2. Roll out the puff pastry, using bench flour to prevent sticking, so that you can cut 2 circles the size of tea saucers out of opposite corners of each sheet of puff pastry: you will have 8 circles in all.

3. Divide the apples among the pastries, and place them on one half of each circle. Be careful not to over stuff. If you have extra apples, fold them into the remaining scraps of puff pastry for a chef's snack. Or if you have extra pastry, cut it into strips and sprinkle with cinnamon sugar and bake alongside the chaussons. For the chaussons, use a pastry brush to paint the egg wash all along the rim of the pastry. Fold over into little semi-circles, and press the edges together. Crimp with a fork. Slice 4 vents in the top of the pastry. Brush with egg wash, and sprinkle with sugar.

4. Transfer the chaussons to 2 baking sheets, and bake for 20 minutes. The pastry will be golden, buttery, and flakey, and the apples will be gooey, oozing, and sweet. Serve warm with cold cinnamon crème fraîche (recipe follows).
5. To make the Cinnamon Crème Fraîche, stir together cinnamon, powdered sugar, and Crème Fraîche. Chill.

1. Rúru rozohrejeme na 205 °C (teplovzdušnú na 185 °C). Jablká olúpeme, vykrojíme jadrovníky a nakrájame na plátky hrubé 1,5 cm. Premiešame ich s 3 PL (44 ml) cukru, 1 PL (15 ml) múky, štipkou soli a šťavou zo 1/4 citróna.
2. Lístkové cesto vyvaľkáme, podsypávajúc múkou, aby sa nelepilo, tak, aby sme z protiľahlých rohov každého plátu mohli vykrojiť 2 kruhy veľké ako čajová podšálka: spolu budeme mať 8 kruhov.

3. Jablká rozdelíme medzi kruhy cesta a uložíme ich na jednu polovicu každého kruhu. Dávame pozor, aby sme ich nepreplnili. Ak nám jablká zvýšia, zabalíme ich do zvyškov lístkového cesta ako maškrtu pre kuchára. Ak nám zvýši cesto, nakrájame ho na pásiky, posypeme škoricovým cukrom a upečieme spolu s taštičkami. Na taštičky potrieme štetcom celý okraj cesta rozšľahaným vajcom. Preložíme na malé polkruhy a okraje stlačíme. Zatlačíme vidličkou. Do vrchu cesta urobíme 4 zárezy na odvetranie. Potrieme vajcom a posypeme cukrom.
4. Taštičky preložíme na 2 plechy a pečieme 20 minút. Cesto bude zlatisté, maslové a lístkové a jablká mäkké, šťavnaté a sladké. Podávame teplé so studenou škoricovou crème fraîche (recept nižšie).
5. Na škoricovú crème fraîche zmiešame škoricu, práškový cukor a crème fraîche. Necháme vychladiť.
